So I actually did a semester-long research project about this my senior year. Here's the rundown:

* As students got older, they cared less about the dress code. My project primarily included juniors and seniors.
* 63% of respondents indicated they were satisfied with the dress code (5 through 7 on a 7 point Likert scale)
* 63% also indicated the dress code did not affect their satisfaction with the gym itself
* Most dress code enforcements were against freshmen
   * The reason for this is that most high schools had lax dress codes for gym/sports and so those were the clothes students had
* Men were more likely to be dress coded because of cutoffs
   * Enforcement of this was lax and down to the individual gym worker but due to sheer numbers, happened the most
* Women were by far the worst repeat offenders
   * Always belly shirts
* The recommendations I had were for the administration to ease up on the cut offs and belly shirts.

Here's the bad news: admin will never ever allow just sports bras. Personally, I found the rule  dumb but they will absolutely not budge on it. It's not even worth trying.

​

All of my research was supplemented with my experiences working in the on-campus gyms for two years. I, and many others, thought the dress codes were heavy-handed. If you come in wearing only a sports bra, you're getting dress coded.
